headline: Corn and beans drift lower as crop progress looms
lead: Corn settled Monday at $4.83 and sits at $4.81¼ overnight, down less than two cents, while beans are off almost a nickel at $12.83. Both markets are flat because USDA's record crop numbers are already priced in, not because anyone expects news today.
teaser: Corn and beans eased overnight while Crop Progress waits for its 3 p.m. slot.

one_number.unit: billion bushels, USDA's corn crop estimate
one_number.context: USDA's October report put corn as the second biggest crop ever and soybeans as the biggest ever, a size the market is still digesting.

sections.title: Grain finds its footing
sections.body:
- Corn is at **$4.81¼** overnight, down slightly after Friday's hard WASDE drop and a Monday session that mostly held steady.
- USDA's own October numbers call for the second biggest corn crop ever and a record soybean crop, so the big supply is already known and priced.
sections.so_what: The market already has the big crop news. Today is about digesting it, not reacting.

sections.title: Cattle and hogs mixed overnight
sections.body:
- Live cattle slipped to **$224.75**, down a tenth of a percent, after climbing for several sessions behind tight feeder supply.
- Feeders eased to $343.48, a pause after recent gains, with no fresh Cattle on Feed data due for weeks.
- Hogs bucked the trend, up seven tenths of a percent to $75.60.
sections.so_what: Cattle cooling off after a run looks like a pause, not a turn.

sections.title: Crude pulls back from Saudi move higher
sections.body:
- WTI crude is at **$91.86** overnight, down 2.0%, pulling back after Saudi Arabia pledged to keep exports flowing despite fresh Houthi missile attacks near Riyadh.
- Saudi Arabia is also moving to expand pipeline capacity that bypasses the Strait of Hormuz, a long-term hedge against the kind of disruption that has pushed prices around all year.
sections.so_what: Saudi Arabia answering supply fears with a pledge, not just words, is why crude eased.

outside_the_pit.title: FSA and UNL host farm safety net webinar Oct. 15
outside_the_pit.body: USDA's Farm Service Agency and the University of Nebraska are holding a webinar on commodity crop safety net programs this Thursday.

watch_list.desc: Crop Progress, delayed a day for Columbus Day; watch harvest pace against the five-year average.
Weekly export sales; corn sales need to hold up against the record crop size.
Corn back above $4.85 would say the Friday WASDE drop is done weighing on the board.

source_summary: CME overnight quotes as of 5:46 a.m. CT; USDA WASDE October report; feedstuffs.com; oilprice.com; thefencepost.com

lines: Corn harvest price so far: $4.96 vs $4.62 projected (+7.4%), 8 of 22 trading days in.
Soybeans harvest price so far: $12.89 vs $11.09 projected (+16.2%), 8 of 22 trading days in.
harvest_clock.note: Average of the daily CBOT settles through Oct 12, figured the way USDA RMA does. RMA posts corn at $4.98. Window and projected price: USDA RMA, as of Oct 12. Oct 1-31 window, most states.
